exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Choosing a Robot Pet
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: I'm thinking of buying that robot dog. It looks so cute.
Leo: Really? Why a robot one and not a real puppy?
Mia: Because it doesn't need to be fed, and it never gets sick.
Leo: That's true. But can it really respond to you like a real dog?
Mia: The shop says it can learn your voice and obey simple commands.
Leo: Sounds impressive. Still, I think a real dog gives you more love.
Mia: Maybe. A robot can't build a true emotional bond with you.
Leo: Exactly. I'd rather have a pet that really feels something.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 想买那只机器狗,觉得它可爱;Leo 问为何不买真小狗;Mia 说机器狗不用喂、不生病;Leo 问它能否像真狗一样回应;Mia 说它能学声音、听简单命令;Leo 觉得很厉害但真狗更有爱;Mia 承认机器无法建立真正情感联系;Leo 表示更想要有真情感的宠物。

options: Learn her voice and obey simple commands.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Worries About New Technology
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A recent report shows that many people are worried about new technology.
Most of all, they are afraid that new machines will make them lose their jobs.
Some say that robots may increase the gap between the rich and the poor.
Many would not ride in a self-driving car without a human in the seat.
Yet the report also notes that technology, used wisely, can save lives and time.
exercises.translation_cn: 一份最新报告显示许多人担忧新科技;他们最害怕新机器让自己失业;有人说机器人可能拉大贫富差距;许多人不愿乘坐没有人在驾驶座的自动驾驶车;但报告也指出,明智地使用科技能挽救生命、节省时间。

questions.stem: What are people most afraid of, according to the report?

options: The gap between rich and poor.

questions.stem: What would many people not do?
options: Ride in a self-driving car with no human in the seat.

questions.stem: What does the report also note about technology?
options: Used wisely, it can save lives and time.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the report?
options: All new technology should be banned.
People worry about technology but it can also help.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Surgery from Far Away
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Nina: Did you hear that a doctor did a heart operation from another city?
Sam: From another city? How is that even possible?
Nina: He used a 5G connection to direct the local team in real time.
Sam: So the specialist didn't have to travel to the patient at all?
Nina: Right. He just needed a fast and stable Internet link.
Sam: But what if the signal had a delay? That sounds risky.
Nina: With 5G the delay is only about one millisecond, so it's safe.
Sam: Amazing. That could really help patients in remote places.
exercises.translation_cn: Nina 说一位医生从另一座城市做了心脏手术;Sam 惊讶问怎么可能;Nina 说他用5G实时指挥当地团队;Sam 问专家因此完全不用奔波;Nina 说对,只需快速稳定的网络;Sam 担心信号延迟有风险;Nina 说5G延迟仅约一毫秒,很安全;Sam 感叹这能真正帮到偏远地区的病人。

questions.stem: Where was the doctor during the operation?
options: In another city, far from the patient.
In the same room as the patient.
On a plane to the hospital.

questions.stem: What did the doctor use to direct the team?
What did the specialist need most?
options: A fast and stable Internet link.

questions.stem: Why is 5G safe enough for this, Nina says?
options: It needs no signal at all.

questions.stem: Who could this technology especially help?

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 How 5G Is Different
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The 5G network is many times faster than the 4G Internet we currently use.
Its biggest advantage is that it greatly reduces signal delay.
With 4G, the delay can be between twenty and eighty milliseconds.
With 5G, the delay drops to about one millisecond.
This small change makes a huge difference when a robot is controlled from far away.
exercises.translation_cn: 5G网络比我们目前使用的4G快很多倍;它最大的优势是大幅减少信号延迟;用4G延迟在20到80毫秒之间;用5G延迟降到约一毫秒;这个微小变化在远程控制机器人时会带来巨大差别。

options: When you watch a film at home.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Setting Up a Smart Home
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Dad: This new speaker is supposed to control all the lights. Can you set it up?
Ella: Sure. You just connect it to the Internet and give it a name.
Dad: And then it really responds when I speak to it?
Ella: Yes. Say "turn on the lights" and watch what happens.
Dad: Wow, the room lit up at once! That's quite impressive.
Ella: You can also use your phone to view the front door from anywhere.
Dad: That's handy. But what happens if the Internet goes down?
Ella: Then nothing smart works, so we still keep the normal switches.
exercises.translation_cn: 爸爸说这个新音箱能控制所有灯,让 Ella 帮忙设置;Ella 说连网并取名即可;爸爸问它真能在他说话时回应吗;Ella 让他说“开灯”看看;爸爸惊喜灯立刻亮了,觉得很厉害;Ella 说还能用手机随处查看前门;爸爸问断网怎么办;Ella 说那时智能功能都失灵,所以仍保留普通开关。

questions.stem: What is the new speaker supposed to control?
options: All the lights in the home.

questions.stem: How do you set up the speaker, Ella says?
options: Take it apart and clean it.

questions.stem: Why do they keep the normal switches?
options: Because the speaker is too loud.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 AI in Everyday Life
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Artificial intelligence is already a quiet part of our daily life.
When you type a message, it guesses the next word you want.
When you open a music app, it recommends songs you may enjoy.
In hospitals, it can study medical images and help doctors find problems.
But AI has no real feelings, so people and machines work best together.
exercises.translation_cn: 人工智能已悄然融入我们的日常生活;打字时它会猜你想用的下一个词;打开音乐App时它推荐你可能喜欢的歌;在医院它能研究医学影像、帮医生发现问题;但AI没有真正的情感,所以人与机器合作效果最好。
